title: Salesforce vs. ServiceNow: Which Agentic AI Stock Is Actually the Better Buy Right Now?
author: Justin Pope
description: Both Salesforce and ServiceNow are leveraging agentic AI to transform their enterprise software businesses amid AI-driven market volatility. While ServiceNow shows faster growth (24.6% annually) with ambitious revenue targets, it trades at a steep 56x earnings multiple. Salesforce, growing at 16.1% annually, offers better value at 18x earnings and represents the safer investment given valuation and margin of safety considerations.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the better buy due to attractive valuation (18x earnings), sticky ecosystem product, strong Agentforce adoption (3.8 billion tasks, 111% quarterly growth), and adequate margin of safety despite slower growth rate of 16.1% annually.

While showing impressive growth prospects (24.6% annually, $30B subscription revenue target by 2030, 30% AI contribution), the stock is considered overvalued at 56x earnings with significant downside risk if AI adoption doesn't materialize as expected.

title: Prediction: U.S. Value Stocks Will Outperform for 10 Years. Which ETFs Should You Buy?
author: Ben Gran
description: Vanguard research forecasts that U.S. value stocks and small-cap stocks will outperform growth stocks over the next 10 years. The article compares two Vanguard ETFs for value stock exposure: the Vanguard Small-Cap Value ETF (VBR), a passively managed fund with ultra-low fees, and the Vanguard U.S. Value Factor ETF (VFVA), an actively managed alternative with broader market-cap exposure. Both funds have recently outperformed the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The fund has delivered 9.51% average annual returns since inception, 27% annualized returns over the past year, and charges an ultra-low 0.05% expense ratio. It combines small-cap and value investing strategies aligned with Vanguard's bullish research forecast.

The actively managed fund has delivered 10.96% annualized returns since inception and 16.9% over the past three years. It offers broader diversification across market caps with a lower P/E ratio (11.4) and has outperformed VBR since inception, though it charges a slightly higher 0.13% expense ratio.

title: ServiceNow Is Down 51% as Wall Street Bets AI Will Gut Its Business. July 22 Will Show Who's Right.
author: Daniel Sparks
description: ServiceNow stock has plummeted 51% from its 52-week high amid fears that AI will disrupt its enterprise software business. However, Q1 results show strong subscription revenue growth of 22% YoY and robust contract metrics, contradicting the disruption thesis. The company's July 22 earnings report will be a critical test of whether the market's pessimism is justified or represents an overreaction.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite the 51% stock decline, Q1 results show strong fundamentals: 22% YoY subscription revenue growth beating guidance, 22.5% cRPO growth, 80% increase in large deals, and 130% YoY growth in AI product customers. The author argues the market's fear is running ahead of facts, and the stock appears undervalued at 24x forward earnings for a 20%+ grower with 44% free cash flow margin.

Mentioned as another software stock dragged down by AI-disruption concerns, trading 40% below its 52-week high. The article uses it as a comparable example of how broad AI anxiety has affected enterprise software valuations.
